source_refs.quoted_text:
Each of the 23 bees in `data/input.csv` occupied its own meadow patch and
contributes exactly one row. The 305 scored departures are not analysed
individually: within a bee the departures are collapsed to a single majority
call (clockwise or counterclockwise), so the analysed sample is one call per
bee.

evidence.description: The data contain repeated within-bee measurements (305 nest departures across 23 bees), which are the only potential source of repeated independent-unit entries; they appear as per-bee summary counts, not as separate rows.

source_refs.quoted_text:
For every bee an observer scored a run of departures from the nest entrance and
noted, for each departure, whether the bee circled clockwise or counterclockwise
before flying off. Those repeated within-bee departures appear in the file only
as two summary counts; the analysis reduces them to a single majority-direction
call for that bee before anything is tested, so no individual departure is ever
treated as its own observation.

evidence.description: The description names bee_id as the independent-unit column and states one line per bee, defining the unit against which repeated-entry would have to be judged.

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one individual mason bee, summarised over all of the nest departures scored for her at her own meadow patch
Independent unit column: bee_id

evidence.description: The report's selected result is an exact binomial test whose count and denominator are bee-level (17 of 23), the quantity that must be checked against the independent-unit definition.

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Exact two-sided binomial test on one majority-direction call per bee: 17/23 bees (0.739) circled clockwise more often than counterclockwise, p = 0.0347; the 50:50 no-bias null is rejected at alpha = 0.05.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by searching for any route through which more than one entry per bee reaches the binomial test: (1) checked whether the test statistic could be departure-level, but the code passes calls.count('clockwise') out of len(calls) where calls has exactly one element per CSV row, and the departure sum is computed only for narrative text, never passed to binomtest; (2) checked for duplicate bee_id rows in data/input.csv, finding 23 distinct IDs B01-B23 across 23 data rows, and the code additionally raises on duplicates; (3) checked whether the reported p = 0.0347 could only arise from a departure-level test, but recomputing by hand gives exactly 17 clockwise-majority bees and a two-sided exact p of 2 * 145499/8388608 ~= 0.0347 for 17/23 at p0 = 0.5, so the reported result is the bee-level test (a departure-level pooled test would use 305 trials, which nothing in the code constructs); (4) checked meadow_patch for shared-unit clustering, but each patch value appears once, matching the stated one-bee-per-patch design. Every attempt failed, so the issue is not demonstrated.
